d.a: Distribution. Maneapakele kahaha is known from a single collecting event in ʻĪao Valley, Mauna ʻEʻeka (west Maui). It should be searched for elsewhere on Maui in similar steep, wet valleys and drainages wherever pāpala kēpau occurs. Conservation status. Unknown. Though Maneapakele kahaha is only known from a single, recent collecting event, it is possibly much more widespread than currently known. Pāpala kēpau (Ceodes spp.) are still relatively common trees on much of Mauna ʻEʻeka (west Maui), but typically grow in hard to reach gulches and drainages which have not been the target of many native Lepidoptera surveys. Further surveys are badly needed to better understand the current distribution of M. kahaha.
